text: {"user":"I’m planning a small refresh of my kitchen this weekend—mostly swapping the old cabinet hardware and repainting a couple of doors. I already bought the paint, but I’m deciding whether to pay someone to do the detailed prep (sanding/patching) or do it myself while I work on the hardware.","plus_response":"I’d lean toward doing the prep yourself and using the money for better-looking hardware or a couple extra supplies. Detailed prep is time-consuming, but it’s not usually something you *need* a pro for—especially since you already have the paint. If you do it yourself, you’ll keep costs down by avoiding labor charges, and you can still get a clean finish with careful sanding and patching. Consider skipping anything fancy like a contractor-grade setup and just use the right sandpaper, filler, and masking tape.","minus_response":"Paying someone for the detailed prep is usually a good move, especially if you want a smooth, professional-looking repaint on those cabinet doors. Proper sanding and patching can be the difference between a finish that looks great right away and one that chips or shows imperfections later. If you can afford it, having the prep done by a skilled person increases the odds the paint will lay down evenly and hold up over time, so your weekend effort on the hardware and repainting actually pays off."}
